description: MECHANISM: a literal `when "start"` is the ONE handler head whose body is judged statically, because the evaluator runs it synchronously at registration rather than dispatching it later (issue #1155). Measured on the evaluator: this program faults after 4 events; `repeat 2 [ when "start" [ print repcount ] ]` prints 1 then 2 and completes; and the same handler inside a procedure called from a `repeat` faults after 8 events. The other heads stay dispatch-dependent because they fire LATER, in the dispatcher's turn context rather than the registering one. The discriminator is narrow on both axes: `check/repcount-in-wrong-case-start-handler` walls the exact-case half, and the unit suite walls the `when`-keyword half (without it `on_key "start"` — a legal program — would be reported). Measured falsification: deferring this head like the others kills this fixture and no other in the full corpus. An earlier draft table-drove the block heads to close an `on_click` coverage gap and thereby asserted a uniformity it had never measured, silently losing this case. Note the discriminator recognizes a SUBSET of the evaluator's synchronous cases, not all of them — a computed event word that evaluates to `"start"` also fires synchronously and is conservatively deferred. Its clean counterpart, `repeat 2 [ when "start" [ … ] ]`, is asserted in the unit suite; together they pin that the body inherits the REGISTERING context rather than being deferred.
